sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2 covers Northwood, a platted but largely unbuilt summer-cottage tract on the north-west shore of Lake Hopatcong in Byram Township. Most of the sheet is a regular grid of long narrow blocks (numbered 34 to 39 and 54 to 58) laid out between Carey Avenue, Isabelle Avenue, Alexandria Avenue, Garside Avenue and Lakeside Avenue, with Hopatcong crossing them as the main cross street; the blocks are marked as forest exposure and carry only scattered frame cottages, many with camp or cottage names. A note on the sheet states that the streets shown, except Lakeside Avenue, are wholly unimproved and impassable for vehicles or fire apparatus. Lakeside Avenue is the one built road: it follows the lake edge from the top of the sheet, passes a cluster of cottages, a dance hall and an ice house, and bends south-west across the lower middle of the sheet towards Allendale Road. Along the shore of Henderson Cove, on the right, a line of wooden piers and boat houses is drawn running out into the water, and the lake and bay are tinted blue. At the bottom the shore of Henderson Bay curves round to Allendale Road and a group of cottages with a wooden pier. The compass rose sits in the middle of block 56. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Insets of islands in Henderson Bay and Henderson Cove (Indian Island, Opitsah Island and others) occupy the lower left and right of the sheet and are separate parts.
notes: Anchored on one junction (Alexandria Avenue / Hopatcong Street), with scale and rotation taken from the atlas scale and the measured lines: low confidence.
Only Alexandria Avenue and Hopatcong Street are used. The modern Isabelle Avenue and Lakeside Avenue lines lie about 10 to 15 m from the streets drawn here and were left out.

The sheet's streets other than Lakeside Avenue were unimproved paper streets; the modern streets of the same names (Hopatcong Street, Alexandria Avenue, Isabelle Avenue, Garside Avenue) follow the plat only in part. Carey Avenue has no modern street of that name.
The name Nigger Brook is printed on the sheet as a historic stream name.
The insets of islands on this sheet are not georeferenced.
The brook name in the place names is the historic name as printed on the 1925 sheet, which contains a racial slur; it is kept only because readings record names exactly as printed.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4 covers Sperry Springs, on the Hopatcong Borough shore of Byram Bay, the western arm of Lake Hopatcong. Maxim Drive is the principal road: it enters at the top left, runs south-east along the bay behind a long row of numbered shore lots (house numbers 801 to 958) and continues to the lower right edge, where it meets Delaware Avenue. The lots between the drive and the water carry cottages, camps and inns with names such as Breeze Inn, Raff Inn, Arrow Head Lodge and Pet Bet Lodge, and a long run of wooden piers and boat houses is drawn along the blue shore. Inland the sheet is mostly open land marked as wooded hillside and forest, with a few scattered houses. At the lower left Du Pont Avenue and Hudson Avenue meet Sutton Road at a five-way crossing near the Sperry Springs post office, and Sutton Road, with A Place (marked arbitrary), serves a small group of camps to the south-east: Camp Rest, Camp Moth, Camp Glencairn and Camp Witten. People's Church and the Franklin stand near the top left. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing slightly to the upper right; the compass rose is in the empty hillside block 87. A separate part at the top right shows Maxim Drive and Delaware Avenue east of the bay, and two small insets of Hopatcong Borough at the lower left are also separate parts.
notes: Anchored on one junction (Hudson Avenue / Maxim Drive), with scale from the atlas and rotation from the measured lines: low confidence.
A hand-picked Hudson Avenue / Sutton Road point (the five-way) is kept in manual/sheet-4-1.json but excluded from the fit.
The modern Dupont Avenue does not follow the Du Pont Avenue drawn here, so it was left out. The modern Delaware Avenue / Maxim Drive junction does not match the drawn one.
A Place is marked arbitrary on the sheet.

sheet-6-3.description: The lower part of sheet 6 covers the south side of the Hopatcong Borough shore at the head of River Styx, from the bridge in the south-west corner eastward along Styx Road. King Avenue, 40 feet wide, comes down the left edge of the part and meets Styx Road and the bridge road at a fork near the bottom left; Bauer enters King Avenue from the west about half way up the left strip, with house numbers 15 along both sides. Styx Road runs east and then north-east across the lower half of the part, with house numbers 401 to 411 and 430 to 459 along it, and the blocks behind it are numbered 105, 106 and 271. Most of the buildings are frame dwellings and summer cottages, many named: Derne Ho., Crossways, Hopatcong Garage, Bon-Air, Clifton, Mai-Bert and Ithanel Ho. (boarding), with Hotel Bon-Air (summer) beside the bridge and G. W. Campbell Est. at the right edge. Crescent Park is a curved row of small cottages numbered 15 to 21 inside the bend of Styx Road. A water tank 25 feet high stands near King Avenue and a reservoir, 30 feet high and filled by pump from the lake, lies near the centre. The shore along the bottom is lined with boat houses, wooden piers and a pier ending in a round platform at the lower left. Heavy lines on the upper right separate this part from the middle inset of the sheet, which shows land cut by lot lines, and from the top part, which is described separately. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Anchored on one junction (the fork of King Avenue, Styx Road and the bridge, matched to today's River Styx Road at Ithanell Road); scale 4.18 px/ft was set from the pilot sheet and rotation measured from the drawn lines. Low confidence.
Drawn King Avenue is today's River Styx Road north of the fork; drawn Styx Road is today's Ithanell Road. Bauer is not in the current street network.
The bridge at the lower left crosses the narrow neck of River Styx; today's North River Styx Road follows it.

River Styx, Hopatcong Borough, 100 ft, three parts: 1 top (King Av, Bauer Arbitrary), 2 middle inset (lots, no street), 3 lower left (King Av = River Styx Road, Styx Rd = Ithanell Road) anchored on their fork, north about -25.

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7 shows the built-up peninsula between two arms of River Styx in Hopatcong Borough, on the west shore of Lake Hopatcong. River Styx Avenue, 40 feet wide, runs the length of the peninsula along its eastern side and ends at a bridge over the river at the top right, drawn running off the sheet to the north-east. At the foot of the sheet it forks: Lakeside Boulevard leaves to the north-east, River Styx Road to the south-east and Lookout Mountain Road to the south-west. Tolles and Irvine Place cross the peninsula from the west shore towards River Styx Avenue, Acme Court is a dashed arbitrary street laid out near the middle of the east side. Most of the peninsula is small frame summer cottages, many named on the sheet (Earlswood, Edgewater, St. George Lodge, Woodcrest, Lynmar Lodge, Highland Court, Stony Hill, Hilltop, Lone Oak), with wooden piers and boat houses along the whole shore. Civic buildings cluster near River Styx Avenue: West Side Chapel (non-denominational), the Hopatcong Theatre (moving pictures), a public school at the fork, and St. Joseph's R.C. Church beside Lakeside Boulevard. The blocks are numbered 109, 110, 113 to 117 and 388. Two strips along Hudson Avenue on the left of the sheet and a part at lower left are separated by heavy lines and are not included here. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Anchored on one junction (the fork at the foot of River Styx Avenue, matched to today's Bell Avenue, Lakeside Boulevard and River Styx Road node); scale 4.18 px/ft from the pilot sheet and north -35 degrees from an overlay of modern roads, not from the printed arrow. Low confidence.
Today's roads leave this junction at other angles than the drawn ones (modern Lakeside Boulevard heads east-south-east, the drawn one north-east), so no second junction was used.

Acme Court is marked ARB. (arbitrary) and drawn dashed. Tolles, Irvine Place and Acme Court are not in the current street network under those names. Highland Court is lettered beside a group of cottages and is read as a building name, not a street.

River Styx Av and Lookout Mountain Rd, Hopatcong Borough, 100 ft. Part 1 main anchored on the River Styx Rd / Lakeside Blvd / Bell Av fork, north -35; parts 2 and 3 strips along Hudson Av on the left. Modern Lakeside Blvd leaves the fork at another angle than drawn.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: lower-left strip along Hudson Av with the River Styx (no street junction; needs carried points or parcel corners).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: top-left strip along Hudson Av, lots 15-30 and 39-49 (no street junction; needs carried points or parcel corners).

sheet-8-1.description: The main part of sheet 8 shows the shore of River Styx and Lake Hopatcong in Hopatcong Borough along Lakeside Boulevard, from the west edge to Pickerel Point and Sharp's Rock. In the upper half Lakeside Boulevard runs east along the foot of a row of deep lots that reach the river, each with a boat house or wooden pier at the water; house numbers 439 to 455 run along it. It then turns south at a sharp bend, passes the compass and the lots numbered 460 to 480, and continues south-south-east towards the bottom of the sheet. Oakwood Drive leaves it on the west near the middle and curves south past a lumber shed and two repair shops. East of the boulevard the land runs out to Pickerel Point and the lake shore, in large estates divided by lot lines and a Private Way: Greystone, Ed. Maurer, Meekston, Hotel Durban (summer) and Hudson Maxim. At the south-east, Sharp's Rock has an observatory and a stone arch bridge with a boat house crossing an arm of the lake. Cottages along the north shore carry names such as Oakdene, Red Croft, Rosemont, Kenilworth, Pactola, Camp Mystic and Cricket Lodge. The blocks are numbered 115, 120, 130 and 131. A strip along the top of the sheet, and an area at lower left west of an inlet, are separate parts divided by heavy lines and are not included here. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Anchored on one junction (Lakeside Boulevard and Oakwood Drive, matched to today's Oakwood Road); scale 4.18 px/ft from the pilot sheet and north -24 degrees from an overlay of modern roads. Low confidence.
Modern Lakeside Boulevard matches the drawn road as far as this junction; south of it today's road turns south-west while the drawn one continues south-south-east, so it was not used as control.
Drawn Oakwood Drive is today's Oakwood Road; Sharp's Rock is today's Sharps Rock Drive area; the printed spelling Pickerel is kept (today's Pickerel Point Drive).

sheet-9-1.description: The main part of sheet 9 covers a small, regular block plan on the west shore of Lake Hopatcong in Hopatcong Borough, which the sheet marks as covering the entire sheet. Hopatchung Road and Shawnee Road run across the sheet and are crossed by Chincopee Avenue, Nariticong Avenue and Lakeside Boulevard; River Styx Road comes in from the west edge and ends at Hopatchung Road just west of Chincopee Avenue, and an unnamed road leaves Lakeside Boulevard towards the north-east corner. Between Nariticong Avenue and Lakeside Boulevard the whole block between Hopatchung and Shawnee roads is Byram Park, left empty. The built-up part is thin: scattered frame cottages and bungalows, most of them named (Knight, Okeden, Glenwood, Dew Drop Inn, Buzunk Lodge, Merrelyn, Hollywood, Chillicothe, Dixie Lodge, Camp Lincoln), lie along Nariticong Avenue, the lots north of Hopatchung Road and the lake side of Lakeside Boulevard. Several of these shore lots have wooden piers and boat houses drawn on the water. East of Lakeside Boulevard the land falls to the lake shore, shown with its blue edge along the right of the sheet, and the south part of the sheet is marked as woods with blocks laid out but hardly built on. Block numbers (151 to 174) are printed in each block, and house numbers along the streets. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right; its lower-left corner holds an inset of another stretch of Lakeside Boulevard, which is described separately.
notes: The north-east corner road from Lakeside Boulevard is not named on the sheet; today Musconetcong Avenue meets Lakeside Boulevard near there.
Chincopee Avenue south of Shawnee Road is drawn dashed (laid out, not opened).

Hopatcong Borough, 100 ft. Part 1: Chincopee Av, Hopatchung Rd, Shawnee Rd, Nariticong Av, Lakeside Blvd, Byram Park (pilot). Part 2: inset lower left, another stretch of Lakeside Blvd with the Hotel Hopatcong (block 173), drawn turned, continues on sheet 4.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset lower left: Lakeside Blvd 801-815 and the Hotel Hopatcong grounds (block 173), continues on sheet 4 (no street junction; stretch of Lakeside Boulevard not identified; needs carried points via sheet 4 inset 3 once placed).

sheet-10-1.description: The main part of sheet 10 covers the south-western end of Lake Hopatcong where Lakeside Boulevard meets the Musconetcong River and the Morris Canal feeder, in Hopatcong Borough and Byram and Roxbury Townships. Lakeside Boulevard, 50 feet wide, runs up the sheet from the bridge at the bottom, with house numbers 1101 to 1137 along it, and is largely open country on either side: the blocks are numbered 177 to 183 and only a few scattered dwellings are drawn, with a vending stand at the road junction. The Hopatcong Country Club, with its club house and the golf course, lies on the left, and a dash-dot line marked as the Byram Township and Hopatcong Borough boundary runs up the left edge. At the foot of the sheet the Musconetcong River crosses from left to right, with the Sussex County and Morris County line marked along it, and the Canal Feeder runs below it parallel; Lakeside Boulevard crosses both on a bridge, and the Old Road to Stanhope, 30 feet wide, leaves it to the west just north of the river. West Shore Boulevard runs south-west across the lower left corner. An inset at the top, a Lakeside Boulevard strip with a milk depot and the borough jail, and the Point Pleasant area to the east are separate parts divided by heavy lines and are not included here. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Anchored on one junction (Lakeside Boulevard at the Musconetcong bridge, with the Old Road to Stanhope, matched to today's Brooklyn - Stanhope Road node); scale 4.18 px/ft from the pilot sheet and north +7 degrees from the road bearing and the printed arrow. The drawn road mouth is wide (about 135 feet) and its centre was taken at the middle, so the position could be 10 to 15 m off. Low confidence.
Today's Lakeside Boulevard north of the bridge curves west of the drawn straight line (about 20 m at 1000 feet), so it was not used as control.
Printed on the road as B'LV'D.; written out as Boulevard.

Musconetcong River outlet, Hopatcong Borough / Byram and Roxbury, 100 ft. sheet-12-1.description: The main part of sheet 12 shows the village of Landing, Roxbury Township, at the southern tip of Lake Hopatcong, where the lake narrows to the outlet of the Morris Canal. The part is L-shaped: it takes in the lower two thirds of the sheet and a strip up the middle, between a large inset at the upper left and a smaller one at the upper right. A broad bundle of Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad tracks runs down the centre of the sheet and passes under a road bridge, with the dry bed of the former Morris Canal beside it. West Shore Boulevard runs north from the bridge along the lake shore, lined with narrow deep lots, frame dwellings, a garage and a few shops; a post office and a shore-front boat landing stand near its south end, and a steamboat landing and a boat basin are drawn on the water to the east. South-east of the bridge Mount Arlington Road runs to a junction with Landing and Mount Arlington Road and Shippenport Road, beside a coal shed and a siding that crosses the road. West of the tracks Old Netcong Road and Dover Road enclose scattered dwellings, a garage with a filling station, a freight house and storage buildings by the station, and a pond. Block numbers 183 to 188 are printed. The compass rose in the lower left points up and to the right. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The two insets at the top, drawn at other angles, are described separately.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (Mount Arlington Boulevard / Shippenport Road, the drawn Mt. Arlington Road / Landing & Mt. Arlington Road / Shippenport Road junction) with the atlas scale and a north direction of 10 degrees checked against an overlay of modern roads; low confidence, anchored part.

Printed Mt. Arlington Road is today Mount Arlington Boulevard; West Shore Boulevard north of the bridge is today's Lakeside Boulevard side of the shore road (modern roads there do not follow the drawn line).
The upper-left inset (Landing and Mt. Arlington Road, Atlas Powder Co.) and the upper-right inset (Shippenport Road, Old Canal Basin) are not placed.

Landing, Roxbury Twp, 100 ft, three parts: 1 main L-shape anchored on Mount Arlington Boulevard / Shippenport Road, north +10; 2 inset upper left (Landing and Mt Arlington Rd, Atlas Powder Co, rail siding); 3 inset upper right (Shippenport Rd, Old Canal Basin).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset upper left: Landing and Mt Arlington Rd, Atlas Powder Co., siding (no street junction; needs carried point from sheet 13).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset upper right: Shippenport Rd, Old Canal Basin (no street junction; needs carried point).

sheet-14-1.description: The main part of sheet 14 shows Bertrand Island and its approach road at Mount Arlington Borough, Roxbury Township, on the east side of Lake Hopatcong. At the top right is the Bertrand Island subdivision, a regular plat of narrow numbered lots in blocks between W. Bertrand Road at the top, Willow, Oak and S. Bertrand Road at the left, with Bertrand Road running as a long diagonal from its south-west corner down the neck of the peninsula. Most lots are empty; frame cottages and a few lodges (Onondaga Lodge, Brownie, Empire Restaurant, Laurel Lodge) are scattered through the plat, and the Lake Hopatcong Yacht Club stands at the north-east corner. South of the plat Bertrand Road passes a carousel and runs down to the amusement area of the Lake Hopatcong Vacation and Outing Co. Inc., with a dance hall, a large block of sleeping quarters called California Lodge, bungalow rows, stores, a boat wharf and a wharf at the shore. The bottom-left corner shows King Road and Bertrand Road with a row of named cottages (Oak Lodge, The Shadows, Jeanne Marie, Sincopated Villa) along the water. Block numbers 260 to 263, 394 and 395 are printed. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper right, and the left side of the sheet is a separately oriented part divided by a heavy line.
notes: Fitted to four junctions of the Bertrand Island plat only, so the fit is local; the fitted scale (3.88 px/ft) is about 7 percent below the atlas constant, i.e. the plat is drawn smaller than today's parcels. Bertrand Road and King Road south of the plat have no control; low confidence.
The part to the left of the heavy line (Windemere Av., Sunset Ter.) is not placed: no street junction.
Modern names: W. Bertrand Road is West Bertrand Road, S. Bertrand Road is South Bertrand Road, Willow and Oak are Willow Street and Oak Street, and Bertrand Road is today Bertrand Island Road.

Bertrand Island, Mount Arlington Borough, 100 ft. Part 1 main: the island plat fitted on 4 junctions at 3.88 px/ft (7 percent under the atlas scale), north +58; part 2 left (Windemere Av, Sunset Ter).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: left of the heavy line: Windemere Av, Sunset Ter (no street junction; needs carried points from sheet 15).

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the centre of Mount Arlington Borough, Roxbury Township, on the east shore of Lake Hopatcong, from the lakefront on the left to the village streets above Tanglewild Glen Park. Mt. Arlington Boulevard and Altenbrand Avenue meet at the middle of the sheet with Windermere Avenue, Dunlap, Park Avenue and Prospect Avenue to the north, forming a small commercial district around the Mt. Arlington Hotel and its annex, Schrefers' Hotel, a Roman Catholic church, an auto repair shop and rows of small stores near the five-way junction at the left. Howard Boulevard (also lettered Mt. Arlington Boulevard) runs east across the sheet. South of N. Glen Avenue the large open tract of Tanglewild Glen Park is enclosed by N. Glen Avenue, S. Glen Avenue and Mountain View Avenue, with Sunset Terrace looping round the lower part. Windermere Avenue follows the lake shore at the left, with scattered cottages and, along the water, many boat houses, a bath house and piers. Along the right side Chestnut Avenue and Howard Boulevard serve a few houses such as Newkirk, Hillside Cottage, Springside, Mountainside and Brookside. Fern Place is marked as not opened, as is part of Dunlap. A heavy double line near the top right edge, with a jog by the compass, cuts off a separately drawn block at the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left.
notes: Placed by five detected junctions fitted to modern streets, with 3 to 8 m residuals and a leave-one-out error of 11 m: the modern street network here differs from the drawn one, so confidence is low. The scale and rotation (4.13 px/ft, north 64 degrees towards the upper left) agree with a manual check against an overlay.

Printed Windermere Av. (not Windemere, as on sheets 14 and 16), Altenbrand Av., Mt. Arlington Blvd., Howard Blvd. (Mt. Arlington Blvd.) are written out; modern Howard Boulevard follows part of the drawn Mt. Arlington Boulevard line.
The block beyond the heavy line at the top right (Chestnut Av., Howard Blvd., blocks 258 to 260) is not placed and is cut out of this part's mask.

Mount Arlington centre, 100 ft, one part (north about -64) plus a NE block beyond a heavy line (Chestnut Av, Howard Blvd, blocks 258-260) cut out of the mask. The modern network does not follow the drawn one closely (RMSE 4 m, LOO 12 m).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: NE block beyond the heavy line: Chestnut Av, Howard Blvd, blocks 258-260 (cut from part 1; no own junction; needs carried points).

sheet-16-1.description: The main part of sheet 16 shows the Alamac Hotel quarter of Mount Arlington, Roxbury Township, on the east shore of Lake Hopatcong. Windemere Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet from left to right, with long narrow lake-front lots running up to the water, a row of boat houses along the shore and scattered cottages and a swimming pool. Arlington Avenue runs south across it, passing the large Alamac Hotel (summer), with its detached laundry, ice house and caretaker's buildings, and carrying on past Hopatcong Avenue, Park Avenue, Rose Place and a baseball park with bowling alleys and a garage down to Mt. Arlington Boulevard. Edgemere Avenue curves round the east side of the hotel grounds along Van Every Cove, passing The Edgemere (a hotel), St. Peters P.E. Church, the Alamac Hotel pumping station and power plant, and Mira Lacum, a large house. Concourse and a second Edgemere Avenue branch lie at the top. Mt. Arlington Boulevard runs diagonally across the lower part with a fire office, a drug store, Hotel Boulevard and a riding academy. Mountain View Avenue, Prospect Avenue and Berkshire Avenue are laid out in the lower left, with houses on only a few lots. Block numbers 229 to 240, 388 and 389 are printed. Two insets of Roxbury Township at the right are described separately. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the right.
notes: Fitted to six junctions (RMSE 1.9 m, leave-one-out 6.4 m, 4.19 px/ft, north 81 degrees clockwise from the top of the sheet). Three junctions were left out because modern streets are displaced from the drawn ones: Hopatcong Avenue (about 8 to 10 m north of its drawn line), Edgemere Avenue at Windemere Avenue and at Rose Place.
The printed street is Windemere Av. (one r), today Windermere Avenue; Mt. Arlington Blvd. is today Howard Boulevard; modern Prospect Street is drawn here as Prospect Av.
The upper-right inset (Summit Av., Chestnut Av.) and the middle-right inset (Berkshire Av.) are separate parts and are not placed.

Alamac Hotel quarter, Mount Arlington, 100 ft. Part 1 main (6 GCPs, north +81); Hopatcong Avenue displaced 8-10 m and excluded; part 2 inset top right (Summit Av, Chestnut Av); part 3 inset middle right (Berkshire Av).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset top right: Summit Av, Chestnut Av (two parallel streets, no junction).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset middle right: Berkshire Av (one street).

sheet-21-1.description: The main part of sheet 21 shows the Castle Rock Park and Homestead Park district on the east shore of Lake Hopatcong, in Jefferson Township. The lake and its narrow arm run down the left edge of the sheet, with boat houses on the shore, and the Lake Hopatcong Branch of the Central Railroad of New Jersey follows the shore beside them before swinging north-east across the top of the part. Dickinson Place runs north from Ridge Road beside the lake, meets Lake Road, and continues north-east as Sterling Place to a junction with Hurdtown Road, which leaves the part at its right edge towards the north-east and south-east. A narrow lane marked Arbitrary Place serves a row of lakeside cottages (The Rocks, Red Roof, Shady Nook and others) south of Lake Road. North of Sterling Place a string of camps and cottages, many named, lines the railroad and the shore, and further north-east cottages stand between the railroad and the lake. Homestead Road curves round the large block marked 215, with Homestead Park lettered across its south side; Willow Avenue and Hurd Avenue cross the south-east, and a group of platted lots lies between Park and Ridge Road in the south-west. Most of the interior is open, unbuilt land. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Two heavy lines divide it from other parts of the sheet: the north-west corner, which shows another stretch of Hurdtown Road at a different angle, and the south-east corner, which shows Homestead Avenue at another angle. The printed compass is not a reliable guide to north here.
notes: Placed from one junction, Castle Rock Road (drawn Dickinson Place) and Lake Road, with the atlas scale and rotation measured from the street lines and checked against an overlay of modern roads and parcels; low confidence, a single point.

Dickinson Place and Sterling Place follow today's Castle Rock Road closely; today's Homestead Road, Willow Drive and the streets east of Castle Rock Road do not match the drawn lines and were not used.
The lane lettered 'Bera Pl. Arbitrary' on the left is read as Bera Place Arbitrary; the lettering is vertical and was read with medium confidence.
The north-west corner (Hurdtown Road at another angle) and the south-east corner (Homestead Avenue) are separate parts and are not covered by this annotation.

Castle Rock Park and Homestead Park, Jefferson Twp, 100 ft, three parts: 1 main anchored on Castle Rock Road / Lake Road (drawn Dickinson Pl / Lake Rd), north +5; 2 top-left inset Hurdtown Rd; 3 bottom-right Homestead Av / Hurd Av.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: top-left inset: Hurdtown Road (no street junction).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: bottom-right: Homestead Av, Hurd Av (no identifiable junction).

sheet-24-1.description: The main part of sheet 24 shows the southern and eastern part of Raccoon Island in Lake Hopatcong, in Jefferson Township. Chincopee Road runs up the spine of the island from the south-west, where it turns west towards Point Breeze at the island's south-west tip, to the north-east, where it bends north towards the part of the island drawn at the top of the sheet; Forest Road leaves it towards the north-west across the middle of the island. The narrow inlet of Indian Harbor separates the western edge of the part from the mainland shore drawn on the left of the sheet, and the open lake surrounds the rest. Development is a scatter of frame cottages and bungalows, several of them named (Kingsley, Highwood, T. J. Moore, Fairview, Sylvan Lodge, Cliff Crest), with boat houses and wharves along the shore, a few small outbuildings and a gasoline pump near Chincopee Road. Block numbers 194, 195 and 196 are printed across the island, with house numbers along Chincopee Road and its westward branch. Much of the interior is left as open, unbuilt land. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned about 20 degrees clockwise from the top of the sheet; two heavy lines divide it from the north part of the island at the top and from the mainland shore of Henderson Cove on the left, which are drawn at other angles and described separately.
notes: Chincopee Road on Raccoon Island is today's Raccoon Island Road; it follows the drawn line closely, including the westward turn near Point Breeze.
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Raccoon Island Road / Forest Road) with the atlas scale and a north direction checked against an overlay of modern roads and parcels; low confidence.

Raccoon Island and Henderson Cove, Jefferson Township, 100 ft, three parts: 1 Raccoon Island south and east (Chincopee Rd = Raccoon Island Road, Forest Rd; north about +20); 2 top, north part of Raccoon Island with Raccoon Rd and Chincopee Rd and Pleasure Bay; 3 left, Henderson Cove shore with Chincopee Rd and Harbor Pl, blocks 190, 192, 345.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: top: north part of Raccoon Island, Raccoon Rd, Chincopee Rd, Pleasure Bay (no junction that exists today; drawn at another angle; distances do not match the modern island; needs carried point from sheet-24-3 or a parcel corner).

sheet-24-3.description: The left part of sheet 24 shows the shore of Henderson Cove on the east side of Lake Hopatcong, in Jefferson Township, at the base of the Raccoon Island peninsula. A heavy line separates it from the north part of Raccoon Island, which is drawn at another angle across a diagonal cut at the upper right, and a second heavy line along the bottom separates it from the main part of the sheet with the southern half of Raccoon Island. The land is a wedge between Henderson Cove on the west and the open lake to the south, with Indian Harbor as a narrow inlet at its south-east corner. A 30-foot road, Chincopee Road, runs down the middle from the top of the part and forks near the lower left. One branch, Harbor Place, leaves to the west towards a boat house on the cove shore, and the other runs south-east towards the lake shore with lot numbers along it. Development is a thin scatter of frame dwellings and outbuildings along the cove shore on block 190, boat houses and a wharf, a house labelled Rex Beach on block 345, and a larger group of buildings in blue near the lake side of block 192 around the premises labelled Dew Drop Lodge. Large parts of blocks 190 and 192 are open woodland marked Forest. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north turned several degrees to the left of the top of the page; the compass drawn on it points further round than the streets do.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction (Chincopee Road forking to Harbor Place, modern Chincopee Road / Henderson Place) with the atlas scale and a north direction of about -20 degrees chosen from an overlay of modern roads and parcels, not from the printed arrow; low confidence, rotation uncertain by a few degrees.

On the overlay the drawn Harbor Place and the south-east branch follow the modern Henderson Place roads within about 30 m, but the straight north arm of Chincopee Road does not: the modern road bends north-east and then follows the cove shore.
The name Henderson Place is today's name of the two branches; Harbor Place is not a modern name.

Raccoon Island and Henderson Cove, Jefferson Township, 100 ft, three parts: 1 Raccoon Island south and east (Chincopee Rd = Raccoon Island Road, Forest Rd; north about +20); 2 top, north part of Raccoon Island with Raccoon Rd and Chincopee Rd and Pleasure Bay; 3 left, Henderson Cove shore with Chincopee Rd and Harbor Pl, blocks 190, 192, 345.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: top: north part of Raccoon Island, Raccoon Rd, Chincopee Rd, Pleasure Bay (no junction that exists today; drawn at another angle; distances do not match the modern island; needs carried point from sheet-24-3 or a parcel corner).

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers the Prospect Point district on the east shore of Lake Hopatcong, Jefferson Township, on the plat of the Prospect Point Land Improvement Company. The lake shore runs down the left side of the sheet from top to bottom and ends in the point at the lower left, where a short road reaches two boat houses on a pier. The rest of the sheet is mostly a paper plat of numbered blocks laid out on a regular grid: Rhode Island, Schwarz Boulevard, New York, Georgia, Pennsylvania and Virginia Avenues run north and south, and Vermont, New Hampshire and Maine cross them. Many of these are marked Not Opened. Building is confined to a scattering of frame dwellings and outbuildings along Maine Street, on blocks 357 to 359, 197, 198 and 199, and along the shore, where a row of small cottages stands on the numbered lots of Prospect Point Camp Sites below Maine Street. The large blocks 202 and 205 east of the point are almost empty, with a few dwellings and a shed beside the diagonal Opper Arbitrary street near the southern shore, where the Prospect Point Land Improvement Co. is lettered. Blocks 346 to 356 at the top repeat the area of sheet 26, to which a match line lettered A to B refers. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north near the top of the page.
notes: Placed by seven detected junctions of Schwartz Boulevard, New York Avenue, Pennsylvania Avenue, Vermont Street, New Hampshire Street and Maine Street; the street names match the modern grid south of Illinois Street.

Today's grid is not labelled as drawn: the sheet's Rhode Island column corresponds to modern New Jersey Avenue and the column printed Georgia Avenue (New Jersey Avenue) to modern South Maryland Avenue, so those columns are not used as control. The sheet's Maine Street is not drawn east of Pennsylvania Avenue.
Most of the streets are marked Not Opened on the sheet; Opper Arbitrary and the shore streets of Prospect Point have no modern equivalent as drawn.

Prospect Point, Jefferson Twp, 100 ft, one part: Schwarz Blvd / New York / Pennsylvania x Vermont / New Hampshire / Maine grid (7 GCPs). Printed column names Rhode Island, Georgia, Virginia do not match today's columns.

sheet-26-2.description: The right part of sheet 26 shows a platted residential tract in Jefferson Township on the east shore of Lake Hopatcong, laid out on a grid of paper streets. It lies to the right of a heavy line that bends from the top of the sheet down to its bottom edge and is drawn with north straight up the page. Schwarz Boulevard and New York Avenue run north and south through it, with the unnamed streets of the plat crossing them, and the cross streets named on the sheet are Lois Arbitrary, Massachusetts and Booth Arbitrary. Numbered lots are shown along the avenues and house numbers run in sequence along them. Development is a thin scatter of dwellings, outbuildings and one large barn or storage building in the upper right, most of it on blocks 337, 338, 347 and 348 either side of Massachusetts Street, and a building named Rock Fern Cottage near Schwarz Boulevard. Blocks 338, 339, 346 to 349 and 351 to 353 are otherwise open. Along the bottom edge a match line lettered A to B refers to sheet 25, which repeats blocks 351 to 353 below it. The sheet carries a 30-foot width for most streets and 50 feet for Schwarz Boulevard. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Placed by four detected junctions (Schwartz Boulevard and New York Avenue with Massachusetts Avenue and Ohio Street); the sheet's Booth Arbitrary is modern Ohio Street. The fit gives 4.1 px per foot against the atlas 4.18 and is medium confidence.
Lois Arbitrary was matched to modern Illinois Street, but the Schwartz Boulevard and Illinois Street junction was left out: it lay about 10 m from the drawn crossing.
The left part of sheet 26 (Woodport Park, Union Turnpike) is drawn at another angle and is not georeferenced.

Prospect Point north and Woodport Park, Jefferson Twp, 100 ft, two parts: 1 left (Woodport Park Dr, Union Turnpike, island 306), turned; 2 right grid (Schwarz Blvd, New York, Massachusetts, Booth = Ohio Street; 4 GCPs).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: left: Woodport Park, Union Turnpike, island 306 (no surviving street junction; drawn at another angle; needs carried points from sheet 26-2).

sheet-27-1.description: The main part of sheet 27 shows Woodport, in Jefferson Township, at the north end of Lake Hopatcong. Union Turnpike runs down the middle of the part from the top, bending near the middle and widening to 50 feet below Prospect Point Road, which enters from the west and is drawn 20 feet wide. A small pond with a few cottages, among them Blossom Cottage, lies east of the turnpike near the top, and the Old Orchard Inn, with notes on its fire protection, stands on the right edge. The inlet of Lake Hopatcong crosses the turnpike by a bridge in the lower right, and Ford Mines Road runs north-east from the turnpike to the edge of the part along the lake's north-eastern arm. Woodport House, a boarding house, and a few scattered dwellings stand along the turnpike; most of the ground is open and the block numbers 44, 45, 46, 47 and 49 are printed across it. A heavy diagonal line runs from the middle of the left side to the bottom edge and separates the part from the Hurdtown ice plant sheet area at the lower left; a second heavy line closes off the strip of Milton Road on the right, and an inset at the upper left shows Hurdtown Road, Juno Arbitrary and Oak View at another angle. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked junction, Union Turnpike (today's NJ 181) and Prospect Point Road, with the atlas scale and a rotation of 25 degrees chosen from an overlay of modern roads; low confidence, a single point.
Prospect Point Road and the northern half of Union Turnpike follow the modern roads closely; south of the junction NJ 181 has been realigned east of the drawn turnpike.
The upper-left inset, the right strip (Milton Road) and the lower-left ice plant area are separate parts and are not covered by this annotation.
